skill.name: User-Initiated Content Load Pattern
skill.description: Micro-interaction where user explicitly triggers new content load via button (e.g., 'Load More' or 'Refresh') with prefetched content to ensure immediate display and avoid surprise layout shifts.
skill.skill_body:
When implementing user-initiated content loading: (1) Prefetch content before the user interaction so it displays immediately upon click. (2) Ensure the user explicitly triggers the load via a clear button or control. (3) Verify that layout shifts occur within 500 milliseconds of user input, which are not counted toward CLS. (4) Test that no unexpected shifts occur after content appears.

## Objective

Enable user control over content loading to prevent unexpected layout shifts and improve perceived performance.
## Applicable Signals

- User expects to control when new content appears
- Prefetching is feasible within the application architecture
- Layout shift elimination is a performance requirement
- Content can be loaded in advance without user awareness

## Contraindications

- Real-time automatic updates are required by the application
- User interaction cannot be added to the content load flow
- Content must load without user awareness or initiation
- Prefetching is not technically feasible or would consume excessive resources

## Intervention Moves

- Add a 'Load More' or 'Refresh' button that user can click to trigger content load
- Prefetch content in the background before user interaction
- Ensure content appears immediately upon user click
- Verify no layout shifts occur after content insertion

## Workflow Steps

- Identify content that will be loaded dynamically
- Implement prefetch mechanism to load content before user interaction
- Create user-facing button or control (e.g., 'Load More', 'Refresh')
- Bind button click to display prefetched content
- Measure layout shift timing relative to user input
- Confirm shifts occur within 500ms window (not counted toward CLS)

## Constraints

- Content must be prefetched before user interaction to ensure immediate display
- User interaction must be explicit and intentional
- Layout shifts must be measured and verified to occur within 500ms of input

## Cautions

- Prefetching may increase initial bandwidth usage; monitor resource consumption
- Ensure button is accessible and clearly communicates its purpose
- Test across network conditions to verify prefetched content loads in time

## Output Contract

- User clicks button; prefetched content appears immediately without layout shift; any shifts that occur are within 500 milliseconds of user input and do not count toward Cumulative Layout Shift (CLS) metric.
